literature_notes: SCARF1 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein: signal peptide 1–19, large extracellular domain 20–421, TM 422–442, intracellular tail 443–830. Both ledger lines (L1, L2) report C-terminal GFP fusions of full-length SCARF1. Because the C-terminus (residue 830) is intracellular, these tags face the cytoplasm and do not qualify as extracellular surface tag sites. No ledger line reports a tag on the extracellular N-terminus (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 19) or anywhere within the extracellular domain (20–421). The extracellular N-terminus (mature residue 20, topology_derived) would in principle be the only surface-accessible terminus, but no ledger line grounds a tag there. Zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GFP fusion of full-length mouse SCARF1 expressed and used in functional studies; the C-terminus (residue 830) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the cell surface.
C-terminal GFP fusion of full-length human SCARF1 transfected into HEK293T cells and used in lipoprotein-binding assays; same intracellular C-terminus, confirmed tolerated but not a surface tag.
